title: Review B3 (T-0018): scorecard build/scores/write, review verdict capture, merge hook, cli scorecard
spec: Adversarial review of the commit(s) on task/T-0018 (your worktree is based on that branch; verify `ls orchestrator/scorecard.py` first). Focus: (1) build() tolerates malformed jsonl lines, missing fields, tasks without executor, and an empty runs dir; keys executors consistently (run field executor vs task executor vs claude:<tier>); (2) scores(): neutral 1.0 below min_runs, success-rate based above, ×0.5 after ≥3 usage-limit hits today; no division by zero; returns a plain dict of floats; (3) merge.py calls scorecard.write inside try/except and a scorecard failure can never change the merge result; (4) spawn.run_worker review path writes review_verdict on both the review task and the reviewed task and does not break when the result JSON has no verdict; (5) executor.start's scores lookup matches what B2 left there (getattr(pool,'scores',dict)()): either scorecard supplies a zero-arg callable or the call site was changed consistently; (6) cli scorecard output: header + one line per executor, --json valid; (7) tests assert behaviour with synthetic runs/tasks under TMP. Run `uv run python -m unittest tests/test_orchestrator.py` and report the result line. Return ONLY {"verdict":"approve|request_changes","comments":[...]} under 3,000 chars.

comments.issue: build() counts review_request_changes on every task file with review_verdict=='request_changes', but spawn.py (run_worker, lines 216 and 219) stamps review_verdict onto BOTH the review task itself and the reviewed (inputs[0]) task. Review tasks have no 'executor' field, so key_of() falls back to f'claude:{tier}', and since bus.create_task defaults tier='sonnet' (bus.py:45), a review done at sonnet tier lands in the same 'claude:sonnet' bucket as real Claude-fallback execute runs. Every request_changes verdict therefore gets double-counted: once correctly on the executor that wrote the code, once spuriously polluting the 'claude:sonnet' bucket's displayed review_request_changes. Doesn't corrupt scores() (which ignores this field) but corrupts the metric `orchestrator scorecard` shows for that bucket. Filter to the reviewed task only, e.g. skip rows where role=='review', or only increment when iterating tasks whose id came from inputs[0].
